page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the DADSv5 server family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and SVM virtualization. The hardware configuration is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the server includes 3686 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ads_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while the single-core CPU performance is strong (top 25%). Memory performance is highly capable, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%) and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 6255.43 GB/sec (top 25%). However, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average category (middle 50%). Cryptographic execution is highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier (top 10%) Passmark CPU encryption test result.

With its high core density, substantial local storage, and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96ads_v5 is well-suited for demanding multi-threaded workloads. It achieves strong results in database operations and Redis SET operations, making it an effective choice for relational databases and caching layers. The instance also handles software compilation and image processing efficiently, scoring in the top 25% and top 10% respectively in Geekbench tests. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a large 3.6 TB local storage allocation provides high resource density for enterprise applications without the added cost of specialized GPU hardware.
description: The Microsoft Azure D96ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) running at 3.7 GHz. It features 384.0 GB of RAM, 3686 GB of local storage, and is Premium Storage capable. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers top-tier (top 10%) multi-core CPU performance and encryption capabilities. Benchmark data shows strong (top 25%) performance in database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. While large-block uncached memory bandwidth and LLM inference speeds remain average, the server's high core density and substantial local storage make it highly efficient for enterprise databases, caching layers, software build pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
